the_population_this_file_declares.rule: Every ET-CC member B2b attributes to the CLIENT leg. The leg is reached as the UNION of the four ticket slices that adjudicated it — CG7 (C1b-i), CG1/CG2/CG4 (C1b-ii), NO CG AT ALL (C1b-iii), and whatever C1a had already tagged — and the union is now the whole leg: every client row in B2b carries a `cg` in {CG7, CG1, CG2, CG4} or carries none, so the four limbs are exhaustive over it. selector.what_this_is: The EXECUTABLE half of `rule`. The generator evaluates it against the source named below and requires the result to be SET-EQUAL, in both directions, to the population this file derives. Prose only becomes a guard when something can run it.
selector.why_it_must_name_a_file_other_than_this_: C1a derived its declared population by unioning the register_keys the edges file itself carried, so a dropped row did not violate the universe, it SHRANK it — measured on MES-99, both a dropped edge and a dropped declared_unmatched row built cleanly at 20 members with every set comparison still exact. A selector that read this file's own rows would be circular by another route.
selector.denotes: 107 ET-CC members — the WHOLE client leg. C1b-i declared 45 (CG7's 29 plus C1a's 18 moved rows, overlapping in 2). C1b-ii added 20 new homes from its 23 CG1/CG2/CG4 rows — three CG2 rows already sat inside the 45 through the `tokens` limb and were not re-homed — taking it to 65. C1b-iii's sub-population, `leg = client AND cg is_null`, is 55 rows and adds 42 new homes, not 55: THIRTEEN of the 55 carry C1a `oc:` tokens and so were already inside through the same `tokens` limb. 65 + 42 = 107. The one-home rule is preserved exactly by not re-homing those thirteen, which is the shape C1b-ii recorded for its three.
selector.why_the_cg_conjunct_and_not_the_whole_cl: HISTORY, kept because the selector's SHAPE is a consequence of it. MES-104 was re-scoped to C1b-i = CG7 at the plan hop, so the leg arrived in three instalments — C1b-i CG7, C1b-ii CG1+CG2+CG4, C1b-iii the members with no CG — and the selector is the union of those slices. The union now covers the leg, and it is NOT collapsed into `leg equals client` for the reason recorded in `why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_slices_and_not_`leg_equals_client``.
selector.why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_sli: The four limbs now denote the whole leg, so `leg equals client` alone would denote the same 107 today — and it is NOT used, deliberately. G22b evaluates `all_of[{leg equals client}]` FRESH against B2b and set-compares it with this file's members. Under a bare-leg top-level selector that comparison would be ENTAILED by G15a's and could never fire: the X7 shape, a guard as empty as one nobody calls. Under the union shape the two ask different questions, and one mutation separates them — add a B2b row with `leg=client, cg="CG9"` and G15a stays green at 107 against 107 while G22b goes red at 108 against 107. That mutation is committed (`crosswalk_controls.exs totality`) and runs in the same run as the unmutated build.
selector.is_null_is_not_get_equals_nil: The `cg is_null` limb is `has_key?(row, "cg") and get(row, "cg") == nil`. Under the weaker `get(row,"cg") == nil` an ABSENT field and a null one are the same thing, so a B2b schema change dropping `cg` would make the limb denote EVERY row and silently re-declare this population as all 281 — reconciling perfectly over a universe nobody chose. As implemented an absent field denotes NOTHING, the denotation collapses, and G15a reds naming every member as `extra`. Measured at this tip: all 281 rows carry the key, so the two readings are indistinguishable on live data and only a unit separates them. Both limbs are unit-tested and the absent-field case is shown separately (`crosswalk_controls.exs selectors`).

the_check_population_this_file_declares.rule: EVERY in-denominator OC check on the CLIENT leg — all 54, across all seven of its scenarios. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed, and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and the reason bucket 2 can now be non-empty. C1a derived its check population from the tags its own edges carried, so bucket 2 — the complement of the edge-bearing checks within it — was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` was a vacuous truth. Declaring the checks from outside the file is what makes the question answerable.

selector.denotes: All 54 in-denominator CLIENT checks — `http-custom-headers` 18 + `http-invalid-tool-headers` 11 (CG7) + `http-standard-headers` 9 (CG1) + `json-schema-ref-no-deref` 1 (CG4) + `request-metadata` 8 + `sep-2322-client-request-state` 5 + `tools_call` 2 (C1b-iii). selector.why_the_locator_artefact_and_not_A1s_man: A1's manifest nests its checks under scenarios and its key is a six-field LIST; the selector's `key_field` must name a string field, and refuses anything else rather than stringifying it. The locator artefact is flat, carries one row per in-denominator check, and already carries the TOKEN — which is the field the edges in this file address checks by, so the two sides are compared in the same unit.

the_check_population_this_file_declares.checks_addressed_outside_it: NONE, now — and that is a RESULT rather than a design. C1b-ii recorded that the 18 moved C1a rows addressed 11 checks in `request-metadata`, `sep-2322-client-request-state` and `tools_call` that no file declared. C1b-iii declares exactly those three scenarios, so those 11 join the declared population and `checks_addressed_outside_the_declared_check_population` falls to 0 for this file. The figure is REPORTED by the generator, not predicted here.
the_check_population_this_file_declares.the_bound_this_leaves: A file could declare a small check population, address many checks outside it, and report a flattering bucket 2. What stops that here is not the arithmetic: it is that the selector names an EXTERNAL anchor by scenario, that every declared check must be axis-decomposed before it counts (the generator refuses otherwise), and that the checks addressed outside are enumerated above rather than left silent. Stated as a residual, not papered over.
the_check_population_this_file_declares.the_9_vs_11_reconciliation: Two figures for CG1 exist and they disagree; stating which is which is the fix, and shipping both in silence is the defect. cg-reconciliation.md §3 records CG1 as MATCHED — 11 check keys, all `http-standard-headers`, 9 SUCCESS + 2 SKIPPED at the accepted run. This file declares 9. The difference is exactly `ClientMcpMethodHeader_initialize` and `ClientMcpMethodHeader_notifications_initialized`, and it is not a discrepancy: 11 is the MANIFEST figure (A1's 175) and 9 is the IN-DENOMINATOR one (the locator's 173, which is the unit this file's selector and every count in it use). Verified at this tip, and the coincidence is worth stating — those two keys are not merely excluded, they are THE WHOLE of A5's exclusion: bucket-0's own arithmetic is `in_denominator 173 + out_of_denominator 2 = 175`, and both of the 2 are these. A5 records each `removed_by_spec` — making them evaluate would need the client to send an `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` request, which 2026-07-28 removed under SEP-2575, so driving them would mean being LESS conformant. They are therefore not available as counterparts BY RULE, and the ET-CC members that would match them do not exist either.
the_check_population_this_file_declares.what_declaring_them_cost: (C1b-iii) G19 refuses a DECLARED check with no axis decomposition, so declaring 15 more checks forced them to be read before any of them could be reported in bucket 2. Eleven already were, from C1a. The FOUR that were not — `sep-2322-client-jsonrpc-id-different`, `sep-2322-client-parallel-isolation`, `sep-2322-default-result-type-complete` and `wire-schema-valid` — were decomposed by C1b-iii into 1, 2, 1 and 1 axes, read at the build and not assumed. That is the mechanism that makes the axis work compulsory rather than diligent, and it is why the declaration and the extraction land in one ticket.

what_a_record_carries_and_why.member: MES-67's unit: module AND test name. The `register_key` is docs/conformance/etcc-row-key.md §1's key and is what joins this file to the register; it was extracted from the register, never typed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim: A3 §1's atom of matching — finer than a test, coarser than an assert. A member bundling claims contributes several edges and they are never collapsed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.tag: A3 §5's token. The generator DECODES and RESOLVES it against A1's manifest and derives the six-field oc_key from the resolution; it never accepts a key from this file.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.axes: One verdict per axis of the check's predicate, naming axes that must exist in the check's axis decomposition (A3's 13 or C1's 11). The generator refuses an axis name the decomposition does not contain — a verdict against an axis nobody extracted is a verdict about nothing.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.et_verdict: The member's own run verdict. Every member of this population is `green`: re-measured at 42e6b19 over the full suite, all 281 ET-CC members pass. So buckets 3 (green OC / red ET) and 6 (red in both) are EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION on this data — checked, and zero, with the predicate recorded.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.evidence: File, line and the assertion, for every axis verdict. Ruling 7: an address is not evidence, the bytes at it are.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.not_carried: No `oc_key`, no `shape`, no `bucket`, no OC verdict. All four are derived — the OC verdict from A1's committed per-check `status` at the accepted run, the rest through MatchKey.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.the_search_that_found_none: On every declared_unmatched record C1b-i and C1b-ii authored: what was read, and what it said. A verdict of 'no counterpart' with no search behind it is a silence wearing a token (A2d). C1a's five inherited records predated this field; C1b-i stated that rather than backfilling, since backfilling would have been inventing the search. C1b-ii RAN the search for the three CG2 ones and added the field to them, attributed and dated in `field_added_by`. The two CG7 records at indices 3 and 4 still predate it and are still left stated rather than invented — their search is a fixture read, and C1b-ii did not run it. C1b-iii authored 37 such records and RAN 17 searches for them, registering each one; and it backfilled the two CG7 records at indices 3 and 4 by running their fixture reads, which is scope beyond its own 55 and was PM-authorised — because G23 is leg-wide, and a guard whose exception list is exactly the rows that would fail it is the defect rather than the remedy.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.why_no_counterpart: Which of the two reason-slugs applies and why. `no-oc-scenario` — the suite has no such check ANYWHERE, so the search is over all 173. `no-oc-fixture-case` — the scenario exists and is matched, but its fixture holds no case that would exercise the constraint, so the search is over the fixture.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: On a bucket-1 record whose search returns zero but where a nearby artefact uses the same WORD in another sense. A zero with its near miss named is a search; a bare zero is a grep that a later reader will re-run, find the word, and mistrust.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim_the_slot_names: MES-77: an `oc:none` native id names a CLAIM, not a member. The field spells that claim out, so the slug is readable and two members discharging one claim is visibly deliberate rather than a collision.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.cg: On a `declared_unmatched` row, B2b's `cg` for that member, carried verbatim so the row says which slice of the cover it came in through. C1b-iii's rows carry `null`, which is not an omission — it is the value B2b holds, and it is what the `cg is_null` selector limb denotes on.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.search_id: On a `declared_unmatched` row C1b-iii authored or backfilled: the `absence_searches` entry whose measurement stands behind this row's zero. The prose `the_search_that_found_none` stays beside it — it is what a reviewer reads — and the id is what a control re-runs.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.why_this_search_is_this_claims_search: The one JUDGEMENT the registry cannot make. A registry entry is a measurement over a population; that THIS member's claim is about what THAT search looked for is a reading, and it is written out per row so it can be disagreed with. Without it a shared search would let a member hide behind a measurement that was never about it.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.authored_by: The ticket that AUTHORED this record, on every record MES-109 added. It exists because the citation audit had been scoping itself to `this ticket's rows` by GUESSING from the tag, and that stopped working here: C1b-iii's `a non-32022 error is never retried` edge carries the same `ClientRetrySupportedVersion` tag as four inherited C1a rows, so no tag predicate can separate them. A field the author writes is the honest way to say who wrote a row; the inherited rows do not carry it and the audit still reports on them rather than going red over work it is not adjudicating.

how_a_silent_axis_was_decided: Conservatively, and the rule is stated rather than applied case by case: a claim counts as covering an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. A test asserting a tool's RESULT does not cover an axis about the ARGUMENTS' wire type, and a test asserting that a capability is ABSENT does not cover an axis about the SHAPE of a present one. This is match-relation.md §6's CG5 rule — a mention is not a discharge — turned on our own side of the relation. Where it was a judgement rather than a reading, the edge's `evidence` says so in those words.
the_all_silent_case: Seven edges have EVERY axis silent, over four distinct checks — this field read `Four edges` until MES-120, which is the CHECK count spent as an EDGE count (measured on MES-117). They are recorded and ESCALATED, never bucketed. A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis 'is no match, not a partial one'; generalised to N axes that is exactly this case, and A3 §3's table has no row for it — `shape_from_axes/1` would call it `:partial` and bucket 5 would swallow it. Dropping the edges instead would be worse: the member would then look edge-less and therefore bucket-1, asserting 'we looked and there is no counterpart' where the truth is 'there is a counterpart and our claim does not touch its predicate'. Escalation is A3 §7's own mechanism for a case the rule does not decide.
what_unmatched_means_in_a_file_that_decl: A3 §6 state 3 reads absolutely — the member has NO OC counterpart. In a file whose check population is a declared subset it can only mean 'no counterpart among the checks this file declares', and the difference is not pedantic. C1b-i recorded two CG7 members whose claims' counterparts lived in CG1's `http-standard-headers`, outside its population; C1b-ii declares CG1, so those are now real edges — which is the mechanism working, and the reason the two kinds of absence were kept apart rather than collapsed. What remains genuinely absent is recorded as such, with the search.
claims_without_an_edge_note: A3's state 3 is a property of a MEMBER, and a member is either edge-bearing or declared unmatched — the generator's bucket-1 reconciliation requires exactly that. So a member that matches on some claims and not on others has nowhere to put the unmatched ones. C1b-i found five and ESCALATED them; whether A3 §6 should gain a claim-level state 3 is MES-110's, not this file's. C1b-ii's disposition of those five, and its own finding, are: TWO became real edges — the tools_call Method and Name claims C1b-i routed here by name, whose counterparts are inside this file's declared 10 now that CG1 is declared. Their claim-level RECORDS were REMOVED, not left beside the new edges: a claim that is both an edge and a claim-without-an-edge is a contradiction in the file, and nothing guards it — `claims_without_an_edge` is reported by count and by row, and a duplicate would have inflated the escalation figure while the edge quietly discharged the same claim. The removal is the completion of C1b-i's routing, and the rows are recoverable from C1b-i's commit (545f48b). TWO were `unowned — recommend it to C1b-ii with CG1`, and C1b-ii ran the search over the real 10 and CONFIRMED both, recording WHY in `resolved_by` rather than passing the recommendation on again; a recommendation no later ticket answers is how these rot. ONE — the SEP-2243 SHOULD-log with no OC check on either leg — is untouched and remains a MES-110 case. C1b-ii adds ONE new case of its own, the no-Mcp-Name-on-a-non-name-bearing-method claim, escalated the same way and not force-bucketed.

The SEARCH REGISTRY. Every `declared_unmatched` row C1b-iii authored, and the two CG7 rows it backfilled, names one of these by `search_id`; the generator refuses a row whose id does not resolve, an entry that records anything but `hits: 0`, an entry with no near miss, and an entry no row names (G23). Each entry carries the SUBJECT searched for at CLAIM granularity, a machine-readable `pattern`, the POPULATION it was run over, the `hits` (0, always — an entry is by definition a search that found none), POSITIVE CONTROLS proving the sweep reached the population, and the NEAR MISS. `crosswalk_controls.exs absence` re-runs every entry's own pattern over its own named population and requires 0, requires each positive control to be non-zero, and requires the `/./s` mutation to match the whole population — so the matcher is shown able to fire rather than assumed to be.

(C1b-iii) WHAT IT TRADES, stated because it is the reason 37 members fit in one ticket. One measurement covers as many as seven members. The per-member statement `my claim's subject is this search's subject` is a JUDGEMENT, not a measurement, and a wrong one hides a member behind a search that was never about it. Two things bound it: the subject is stated at the granularity of the CLAIM (`decode_event/1` field parsing, never `SSE`), and the near miss is per-search — so a member whose nearest check differs from its group's cannot share the group's search and gets its own. That is why S01 and S02 are separate over one pair of SSE rows, and why S13 and S14 are separate inside one `describe` block. The judgement is carried VISIBLY on every row, in `why_this_search_is_this_claims_search`, so it is reviewable rather than implicit.

The 26 `declared_unmatched` rows C1b-i and C1b-ii authored carry a prose `the_search_that_found_none` and NO `search_id`: their searches were run, and recorded, but not registered in a re-runnable form. Registering them would mean either re-running 26 searches C1b-iii did not run, or writing a `hits: 0` nobody re-measured — the invented-field defect C1b-i refused. So G23's PROSE limb is leg-wide with no exception, and its REGISTRY limb reaches the 39 rows that carry an id.
